claims.statement: A news pull is started either by Scout's staff-only run_import_now with sources naming tavily_news (checked before funder_calls and the catalog adapters; it calls _news_pull: select, create_run, execute_run with Deps.from_settings, and records refused items for other named sources) or by `make news-pull`, which runs app.ingest.news.run and uses the same plan_for, create_run and execute_run. The plan is shared by plan_import (via _news_plan_line), GET /ingest/news-runs/plan and the CLI through pipeline.plan_for.

Pull scope is explicit: with no names and no feeds a run covers everyone plus all topic feeds, with names it covers only matching Registry records, and feeds-only runs pull just the feeds. Unknown feed keys are refused (422 on the plan route), and the CLI refuses an everyone-pull without CONFIRM and any ORG/FUNDER that matches nothing. create_run records 'all' as an explicit sentinel and _parse refuses a run naming nobody.

Run lifecycle: create_run sweeps news runs stuck running past 35 minutes to failed; execute_run claims the run atomically via claimed_at (a concurrent execute raises RunBusy, a stale claim is marked failed), and _finish only updates runs still running. If every subject's search fails the run ends failed, and subjects with any failure keep their news_watch watermark so the next run retries them; only failure-free subjects have advance_watch called.

Searching uses Tavily (topic=news, advanced depth, three attempts) with, per subject, up to four quoted queries (name, district variant for ambiguous names, aliases and namesake-file spellings) each run over an open-web scope and an allowlist scope; the window is 90 days for a newcomer else days since the watermark, and items before a stale floor (90 days back for a newcomer, else 30 days before the watermark) are scored links but never stories.

Classification is one structured model call per (link, subject) at PROMPT_VERSION signals-v2, run on the utility (Haiku) model; pairs already scored at that version, duplicate URLs, profile/directory/job pages and items dated before the floor are skipped. A per-run cap (news_max_classify, 2000) refuses the overflow and holds those watermarks, and each verdict is saved as it lands so a killed run keeps its work.

Model tiers by stage: Scout supervisor and Ask use MODEL (Opus), per-link entity/topic classification and headline writing use UTILITY_MODEL (Haiku), story grouping uses RESEARCH_MODEL (Sonnet) with json_schema structured output because forced tool calls are unsupported on that tier, and the verifier agent uses RESEARCH_MODEL with a fallback to MODEL.

The verifier is off while NEWS_VERIFY_MAX=0 (the default): Deps.from_settings only builds it when news_verify_max > 0, and _Checks.settle returns the first read unchanged when no verifier exists. The plan line shows 'up to N checks' and their cost only when checks are non-zero.

needs_check selects only entity-subject news matches near the public bar: news_verify_low (0.35) <= match < public_match, or negative stance with listed_match <= match < negative_match. Each check spends from news_verify_max, runs behind news_parallel_verify slots, and is bounded by a run-wide news_verify_seconds deadline plus a 120 s per-check timeout; over-cap, out-of-time, timeout, failure or no verdict keeps the first read and logs a news_verify item as refused, otherwise matched or updated (updated when match moved by more than 0.15, recording old/new values).

The verifier is a read-only deep agent (read_page, search_public_sources, read_file floor; no subagents, no checkpointer) limited by ReadingLimit (3 page reads) and call_limit (8 calls), returning a slim Check merged onto the first read with verified=True. A check may raise match, confidence or flip on_target only if read_page actually returned the page named in evidence_url; otherwise the first read's values stand and the evidence is annotated, so injected page text cannot lift a score unread.

Stories are built from stored scores (store.unstoried returns on-target links at or above the listed match bar not yet in a story for that subject), feeds first, so a crash resumes. group.group does an exact URL/title pass then a Sonnet merge with recent stored stories, falling back to the exact pass on model failure and allowing at most one stored story per group; each story is written in a single transaction.

Visibility bars are applied in code from Settings: an entity link is public at match>=0.7 and confidence>=0.9 (0.9/0.95 for negative stance) when the story is news, listed at 0.6/0.8, otherwise hidden; an undated non-news item is hidden. A topic story is listed only if match>=news_topic_match (0.75), news, dated and not international, and stays listed once listed. upsert_entity_link only overwrites when the new (match, confidence) is at least the old one and keeps staff-hidden links hidden; recompute_visibility (make news-visibility) rewrites visibility from stored scores but leaves staff-hidden rows.

Migration 0044_news.sql defines news_stories, news_links (URL unique, snippet only), news_link_scores (one per link, subject and prompt_version, verdict jsonb), news_story_entities, news_story_locations, news_story_tags and news_watch, plus ingest_runs.claimed_at. RLS lets anon see only public entity links, signed-in users public and listed ones (staff everything), and restricts news_link_scores and news_watch to staff; the pipeline writes as the owner and hiding goes through a staff route.

Ask's SQL catalog (backend/app/ask/tools/sql/catalog.py) exposes news_stories, news_links, news_story_entities, news_story_locations and news_story_tags (news ids cite [news:N]) while news_link_scores, news_watch, ingest_runs and ingest_run_items are in KNOWN_EXCLUDED, so verifier evidence and watermarks are not queryable from Ask.

The Ask news-brief skill (backend/app/ask/skills/news-brief/SKILL.md), loaded via rule 13 of the Ask instructions, reads public, is_news stories from news_story_entities joined to news_stories (30 days default), reports zero results as 'Nothing on <name> in Sangam's news since <date>' using max(fetched_at) from news_links, gives the story's main link as-is (it cannot read the page, so it never says what the article cites) for negative-stance or fcra/governance stories, and writes three to five lines with [news:N] citations and High/Medium/Low levels.

REST surface: GET /news/stories (caller-run so RLS governs it, keyset-paged by match, confidence, date, with three bucket counts capped at 501; area defaults to all for staff and mine otherwise; last_pull read via the owner pool), GET /orgs/{slug}/news and /funders/{slug}/news (public entity links only), profile endpoints that embed the same entity_news read with a failure-tolerant empty fallback, POST /news/stories/{id}/hide (staff, exactly one of org_id or funder_id, 404 if no such link) and the staff-only GET /ingest/news-runs/plan.

UI surfaces: the Media & Signals view (MediaView/StoryCard) with org, funder and general buckets and a staff hide action; the Registry profile 'News & social' tab, where OrgProfileTabs and FunderProfileTabs mount NewsSocial with profile.news and SQL-derived press/social counts; and the Scout ImportApproval card, rendered via useInterrupt while run_import_now is paused, which has news, open-calls and generic variants, and only the news variant fetches /api/ingest/news-runs/plan (names and feeds) to show coverage, searches, checks and cost before approval, degrading to a notice if the fetch fails.

Test coverage focuses on run mechanics in test_news_pipeline.py (integration: repeat pulls, watermarks, double execute, stale claims, caps, story atomicity), with store, SQL, RLS, route, Scout-tool and CLI tests alongside; no test exercises needs_check or the verifier, and the pipeline test's Deps leave the verifier off.

gdelt and india_csr are parked sources: asking for one by name records a refused run item carrying the PARKED reason, and their adapter code is gone; a news pull runs alone and other sources named alongside it get refused items.

The news-run form routes are removed: only the staff-only GET /ingest/news-runs/plan remains (non-staff get 403), so a news pull can be started only through Scout's run_import_now or the CLI. runner.runnable_for excludes tavily_news unless a source list names it, because a news pull costs money.
